investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T18:23:52Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the inner swarm error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs at the very first API call — agent creation — no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a total contract gap for the remote-agent-create check.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected every POST /api/agents request with HTTP 409 because the eval org has reached its remote agent quota limit of 100. The creation call fails before any agent identity or VM state is established, so all downstream checks (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) that depend on a successfully created agent inherit the same failure message. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary — Eval org remote agent quota exhausted at the swarm layer: the 409 body explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', meaning the org used by the status probes has accumulated 100 remote agents and the swarm backend refuses new creation requests until existing agents are deleted or the quota is raised.

Lower confidence — Eval org shared with non-eval workloads: if the org used by the status probes is also used for manual or automated non-eval agent creation, external activity could consume quota independently of the probe runs.

Because the session could not be opened, the stream never emitted a generation_completed frame nor an image artifact URL, causing both required contract assertions to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime endpoint targeted by the /api/generate/image/stream SSE probe returned a 404 during session establishment (error code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED). This is an eval-infrastructure or backend-routing failure localized to the production-api runtime environment: the harness was either not deployed, deployed at a different URL than configured in LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL, or running an incompatible version that does not expose the expected endpoint. The stream was terminated before any generation work could begin, so no generation_completed frame or image URL was ever produced. This is an eval-level failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so no claim of a user-facing outage is made. The check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational for the production-api environment (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:237-245), limiting its status-page impact.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T18:23:52Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the inner swarm error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs at the very first API call — agent creation — no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a total contract gap for the remote-agent-create check.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected every POST /api/agents request with HTTP 409 because the eval org has reached its remote agent quota limit of 100. The creation call fails before any agent identity or VM state is established, so all downstream checks (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) that depend on a successfully created agent inherit the same failure message. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary — Eval org remote agent quota exhausted at the swarm layer: the 409 body explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', meaning the org used by the status probes has accumulated 100 remote agents and the swarm backend refuses new creation requests until existing agents are deleted or the quota is raised.

Secondary — Leaked eval agents from prior probe runs: if the withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs failed to delete previously created remote agents (e.g., due to earlier probe crashes or cleanup errors), those agents would accumulate against the quota over time, eventually exhausting it.

Tertiary — Quota limit misconfigured or lowered for the eval org: the swarm backend quota for the probe org may have been set or reduced to a value that the normal volume of eval runs can exhaust, rather than a higher limit appropriate for automated testing.

Lower confidence — Eval org shared with non-eval workloads: if the org used by the status probes is also used for manual or automated non-eval agent creation, external activity could consume quota independently of the probe runs.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on /api/generate/image/stream in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint was unreachable at the time of the probe. Because the session could not be opened, the stream never emitted a generation_completed frame nor an image artifact URL, causing both required contract assertions to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime endpoint targeted by the /api/generate/image/stream SSE probe returned a 404 during session establishment (error code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED). This is an eval-infrastructure or backend-routing failure localized to the production-api runtime environment: the harness was either not deployed, deployed at a different URL than configured in LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL, or running an incompatible version that does not expose the expected endpoint. The stream was terminated before any generation work could begin, so no generation_completed frame or image URL was ever produced. This is an eval-level failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so no claim of a user-facing outage is made. The check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational for the production-api environment (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:237-245), limiting its status-page impact.
